title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Release Log. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Release Log
options.lineage: best-in-class product changelogs and release histories
options.thesis: Your whole library is one versioned release history: every project ships, and every post is a release note.
options.viewport: Name and a one-line intro, then the log starting at Now, with a dated row for each project and post on one rail.
options.risk: Changelog grammar can read like a product company; the voice and the cross-links have to keep it personal.

raised.raise: Focusing any entry draws leader lines along the rail to every linked project or post, so the relationships are visible rather than buried in footers.
Every layout decision snaps to whole rail units; there are no fractional offsets.
Motion uses real spring physics with mass and damping for expand and collapse, never linear fades.
Full keyboard operation: j/k walks the log, Enter expands, and / filters.
Type-scale courage: the newest entry's title is set an order of magnitude larger than the archive's.

options.label: The Workspace
options.lineage: Linear, Raycast and Things-grade app shells
options.thesis: The library as a calm, keyboard-first app: projects and posts as one database with views.
options.viewport: App shell with a rail on the left and a unified library list in the canvas, filters as chips.
options.risk: Familiar: it's close to the Synthesis tile and to where most runs for builder portfolios land.

options.label: Patent Sheet
options.thesis: Each project is a numbered figure; its parts link by leader lines to the writing that explains them.
options.viewport: Fig. 1, the library: entries as numbered figures on a ruled sheet, with carmine marking what's under examination.
options.case: Builders identify with technical drawings, and project-to-writing links map cleanly to numerals; it loses on clarity for quick skimming.
options.risk: Without real diagrams for each project it slides into costume, which is gimmick over content.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: A library as a force network of linked works.
options.viewport: A breathing strut network with entries at nodes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the visitor came to browse and read, not trace loads.
options.risk: Navigation by force diagram hides content.

options.label: Azulejo Hall
options.thesis: Works as painted tile panels in cobalt.
options.viewport: A framed cobalt panel per project.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to the audience's world.
options.risk: Pure costume for a software library.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Entries as channels, with activity as needles.
options.viewport: A row of meters, one per project.
options.case: Fuses poorly: there are no real signals to meter.
options.risk: Invents metrics the library doesn't have.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The library as a text-mode board with numbered exits.
options.viewport: Title art over numbered menu lines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nostalgic costume, which you steered away from.
options.risk: Reads as a theme, not a person.

options.label: Merz Collage
options.thesis: Works as torn scraps pasted at angles.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The classic builder portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and intro, a grid of project cards, then recent writing.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev portfolio by design.
